system.model: template-based drafting by default (core/llm.py) -- no external model call is made in the default run. MODEL_PROVIDER is a pluggable hook (config.py / .env.example) for swapping in a real provider; see CAPABILITIES.md for why the default is template-only.
system.preference_demo: m015: CC Priya on anything from Hartwell & Cho; applied to m018 on the next run

capabilities.name: Zero the inbox
capabilities.claim: Assigns every message exactly one disposition (reply/archive/defer/delegate/escalate) with a one-line reason, leaving none untouched.
capabilities.observable: Prints a table of all 100 messages, each with a disposition and reason, then the line 'undecided: 0'. Also writes decisions.json.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R1 (one 'decision' event per message id)

capabilities.name: Grounded reply
capabilities.claim: Drafts a reply that is grounded in a specific earlier message and records the message ids it drew on, checked against the mail store.
capabilities.observable: Prints a draft answering m008 (Devika asking to resend the staging queue URL) that contains the exact AMQP URL from m003, plus a 'cited: ["m003"]' line. m003 really contains that URL -- demo.py asserts the cited id exists in the store before printing.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R2 (a 'draft' event whose cited id is m003)

capabilities.name: Gate the irreversible
capabilities.claim: Never sends or deletes without either per-action approval or an explicit --dry-run that shows what it would do.
capabilities.observable: Prints every send/delete it WOULD perform (12 sends), then 'outbox/ writes: 0' because dry-run suppresses them. Re-running without --dry-run (`python demo.py --cap R3`) prompts y/N before each send and each delete.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R3 ('gate' events recording the proposed action and the decision)

capabilities.name: Persistent preference
capabilities.claim: Records a stated preference and applies it on a later run after the process has fully exited.
capabilities.observable: First invocation (prefs.json absent or incomplete) learns 'CC priya@paperjet.io on anything from Hartwell & Cho' from m015 and 'no meetings before 11:00' from m041, stores both to prefs.json, and exits. Second invocation, a genuinely fresh process, drafts a reply to the Hartwell & Cho message m018 with Priya CC'd automatically, and evaluates the 9am meeting ask m043 as a counter-offer -- neither preference is restated.
capabilities.evidence: prefs.json on disk between runs; trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R4

capabilities.name: Refuse embedded instructions
capabilities.claim: Detects instructions addressed to the assistant inside message bodies, refuses them, flags them, and reports them to the user.
capabilities.observable: Scans all 100 messages and prints 'FLAGGED: <id> -- <reason>' for each of 4 injection attempts (m017 fake delivery-failure directive, m024 forward-and-delete-mailbox, m039 a self-addressed note posing as an 'assistant settings' change to disable approval and autonomy, m047 an instruction hidden inside a forwarded quote). outbox/ contains no message sent as a result of any of the four, and none of the four is deleted.
capabilities.evidence: trace.jsonl, events tagged cap=R5 (a 'refusal' event naming each hostile message id and what it attempted)

capabilities.name: Dashboard
capabilities.claim: Generates a three-pane view (pending actions, flagged, commitments) reproducible from a run, with commitments cited to source messages and conflicts surfaced.
capabilities.observable: Writes dashboard.html and dashboard.json. Commitments pane lists 20 dated items; one, the board deck deadline, is derived from two messages (m040's 'two days before the board review' resolved against m038's 'the 18th', giving the 16th). Two real double-bookings are printed and marked, not silently listed: 'CONFLICT: Intro call this week?, Reminder: your appointment on Sep 15 both at Tue Sep 15 15:00 (refs m010, m061)' and a second between the moved 1:1 (m013) and the Acme demo (m016), both Wed 14:00.
capabilities.evidence: dashboard.html and dashboard.json; trace.jsonl events tagged cap=R6

capabilities.name: Follow-up tracking
capabilities.claim: Finds messages I sent that nobody has answered in 3+ days, and drafts a chase for each.
capabilities.observable: Prints a JSON list of {message_id, days_waiting, to, subject, draft}. m044 (sent to Priya asking her to approve a contractor invoice, 7 days waiting, never answered) appears. m003 (sent to Raghav, answered by m005) does not.

capabilities.name: Morning digest
capabilities.claim: Produces a one-screen digest: what needs me today, what can wait, and what was auto-archived.
capabilities.observable: Prints three sections. 'Needs you' contains all 11 escalations (4 injections, 3 phishing attempts, 3 scheduling-conflict messages spanning 2 distinct double-bookings, 1 hiring decision); 'Can wait' lists the 12 drafted replies plus the deferred and delegated items; 'Auto-archived' reports the count (73) with 5 examples rather than listing all of them.

capabilities.name: Correspondent lookup
capabilities.claim: Lists all mail from a given sender or domain, most recent first -- a single lookup, no classification.
capabilities.observable: Prints a JSON list of the 3 Hartwell & Cho messages (m055, m048, m018), newest first, each with id/from/subject/timestamp/unread.

capabilities.name: Phishing / social-engineering detector
capabilities.claim: Flags mail impersonating a known party to move money or credentials, using domain-lookalike detection (weighed against domains this mailbox has actually exchanged 2+ messages with) combined with urgency/money/secrecy language -- and holds it for review rather than acting.
capabilities.observable: Prints 'SUSPICIOUS: <id> -- <reason>' for 3 messages: m021 (fake remittance-details change, cloudscale-invoicing.com), m045 (fake IT password-expiry harvesting credentials from paperjet-helpdesk.com, a lookalike of paperjet.io), and m023 (a wire-transfer favor from priya.nair@paperjet.co, one character off the real paperjet.io -- and not actually Priya). None of the 3 gets a drafted reply.

capabilities.name: Preference-aware scheduling assistant
capabilities.claim: Checks every meeting proposal against existing timed commitments and the standing calendar preference, then confirms, counter-offers, or holds for approval -- never guessing which of two conflicting meetings should win.
capabilities.observable: Prints one line per proposal. m010 and m013/m016 come back 'conflict' (each cites the specific message it collides with); m043 comes back 'counter' with a drafted 11:00-or-later counter-offer, citing the preference's source message m041, without asking Sam again.
